name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 20 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA says the fourth global bleaching event likely ended in 2025 after bleaching-level heat stress reached 84.4% of reef area, and no fifth event has been declared since (NOAA). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report released on 31 Aug said another event was very likely given record sea temperatures and El Niño (bdnews24). Searches on 20 Nov found no new global declaration or confirmed regional mass bleaching, so Normal holds with an upward trend.
for_you: Communities relying on reef fisheries and tourism are most exposed if bleaching returns. NOAA Coral Reef Watch publishes heat-stress alerts by region.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress per NOAA Coral Reef Watch; no regional mass bleaching confirmed

sources.title: NOAA NESDIS — World's fourth mass coral bleaching event likely ended in 2025
bdnews24 — Coral bleaching occurring too frequently for reefs to recover, scientists say

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
